text:
ANOTHER SPECIMEN OF THE INVARIANT-FAMILY PROBLEM, and this one has real consequences rather than merely wasting time.

A user whose relation was built from precomputed effects asks for any residual-based quantity and receives, for all four accessors:

  Relation-fit fields are missing or noncanonical.

Nothing is missing or noncanonical. The relation is perfectly well formed; it simply carries no error channel, because it was built from betas rather than from responses. The message describes an internal structural check and names neither the cause nor the remedy.

What the user needs to be told is that this relation was built from precomputed effects and therefore has no residual information, that lm_relation_fit() is the constructor that retains it, and - given the SE finding on bd-01KZY9FGVJ0JXCB1Q1KN88AE6D - that on this path a correct standard error is not computable inside the package at all and subject-level resampling is the alternative.

This is the clearest case yet for the split proposed on this bead. 'Fields are missing or noncanonical' is the phrasing of an internal assertion. Here it is the ONLY thing standing between a user and the knowledge that their chosen entry path forecloses correct uncertainty estimation. A user reading it will reasonably conclude they constructed the object incorrectly and go looking for the mistake.
